evidence: Traupman 147: bella et venusta (pretty and attractive)
terms.comment: Lovely and graceful, of people, things and speech, from Venus; Cicero’s venustās is the womanly kind of beauty (see beauty).
Finely formed: the plain word for a good-looking man or woman (see pretty).
Worth loving, delightful, of a person’s whole manner rather than of looks.
Not in Cicero in this sense; common only after Augustus. Of reasons and pretexts, it is plausible, specious (Cic. Att. 16.7.6; Lewis & Short).

terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; in Cicero very rare, and then in a bad sense, dainty (Lewis & Short)
evidence: Ter. And. 5.4.45: Ō lepidum patrem! (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Lewis & Short: mostly of places and things that please the senses; of people less often.

phrases.latin: eamque quam numquam vīdī tamen et amō et amābilem esse certō sciō
phrases.english: and though I have never seen her, I love her all the same, and I know for sure that she is charming
